source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Socket0/errortype3 lack vendor mapping; threshold FF5/FFE relevance is unexplained. SyncFlood has no pre-state/clear/freshness rule, and no CPU-WDT-specific record or CPU/core recovery criteria distinguish this case from DF IOM/CCM watchdogs. OS execution method, deadlines and RDIMM relevance remain incomplete.

review_improvement: Adds CPU-WDT-specific durable attribution and CPU/core recovery, preventing a generic watchdog log or stale SyncFlood bit from satisfying this distinct processor-source test.
independent_technical_reasoning: A CPU watchdog can reset the platform yet leave a package, core set or MCA state degraded, so successful reboot alone is insufficient. The same --dferror family is used for IOM and CCM in adjacent rows, while a sticky SyncFlood bit can predate this injection. Therefore errortype3 needs vendor proof and fresh CPER/MCA identifiers tied to the intended CPU target, followed by topology and workload health checks.
